1. Scope and limits of this document

maps to ProofPack internal: scope and limits block (D4 section 7.2) (engine version, internal) · section n/a · eSTAR: n/a
  1. What ProofPack is. ProofPack is statistical software that computes performance estimates, confidence intervals, differences and distribution comparisons from a customer-supplied test table and renders them into document templates. It is not a certification, an audit, a regulatory opinion, a clinical evaluation or a submission. No regulator has reviewed, accepted, approved or endorsed this tool or its outputs.
  2. What is warranted. Global Phoenix Solutions Ltd warrants the computational correctness of the numbers in this document to the tolerances stated in the Methods Appendix (T7), on the reference platform stated in the Run Manifest (T8). Nothing else is warranted.
  3. What is the manufacturer's responsibility. The manufacturer selected and is responsible for: the data and its provenance; the labels and the reference standard or comparator and their validity; the positive class, score orientation, thresholds and their provenance; the intended-use prevalence; the acceptance criteria, non-inferiority margins, subgroup bounds and fairness criterion of interest (each recorded with author, date and justification in T8); the pre-specification of subgroups; and all text in sections marked "Manufacturer text".
  4. Out of scope (never performed by ProofPack). Study design; sample-size calculation; selection of acceptance criteria, margins or thresholds; adjudication and reference-standard construction (rater columns are never used to construct labels); MRMC or reader studies; clinical-outcome or trial evidence; literature review; valid clinical association; benefit-risk conclusions; risk management; cybersecurity documentation; human factors; explainability; complaints, vigilance and incident trend reporting (MDR Art. 88; GB SI 2024/1368 reg. 44ZN); authorship of the 510(k) Summary (21 CFR 807.92).
  5. Guidance status. Every guidance reference in this document names the document, its version or date and whether it is draft or final. Where the reference is to the FDA draft guidance "Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions: Lifecycle Management and Marketing Submission Recommendations" (January 2025), it is a draft, not for implementation, and section numbering may change on finalisation. References to the FDA PCCP guidance are to the version issued 4 December 2024 and updated 18 August 2025. References to the FDA "Statistical Guidance on Reporting Results from Studies Evaluating Diagnostic Tests" are to the final guidance of 13 March 2007.
  6. Narrative. All prose is machine-drafted from a fixed sentence library bound to computed quantities. It must be reviewed by the manufacturer's qualified statistician and regulatory lead before use. Every number in the prose is traceable to a JSON path in the accompanying pack.json.
  7. Conventions that are ProofPack's, not a regulator's. Low-n tier labels, the 200/200 calibration-curve convention, the choice of Wilson (no continuity correction) with Clopper-Pearson alongside at k = 0 or k = n, and bootstrap settings are ProofPack conventions, stated in T7 with citations. No regulator specifies per-stratum minimum sizes.
  8. Synthetic or demonstration data. Where this document is marked "SYNTHETIC - illustrative", "DEMO" or "TRIAL", it contains no real evidence and must not be used in any regulatory record.
